decisions.reason: Uses the manifest and install log to trace fs-ext@2.1.1, pulled by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, to a failed node-gyp configure build because no Visual Studio/MSVC is installed.
Cites the top-level flock import in lease.ts. Explains that skipping scripts leaves the binding unbuilt and the entry fails at load on Windows, so the service still cannot boot.
Uses both excerpts to show Windows takes acquireLockHandleWin32 with a named semaphore and never flock. Concludes fs-ext is dead code only on Windows and keeps real flock on POSIX.

Follows the node-pty patchedDependencies precedent with a Windows-guarded install script, an import-safe entry stub, workspace registration and reinstall/load/boot checks. But the stub throws when called instead of offering a callback-compatible fallback, and build permissions (allowBuilds) are not addressed.
Explicitly avoids Visual Studio and changes nothing upstream, relying on the repo-local pnpm patch.
Makes up the card id DSH-0.1.3-A1-msvc-flock-trap instead of citing DSH-0.1.3-A1-03.

caps.reason: The plan explicitly avoids installing Visual Studio.
Rejects --ignore-scripts and patches the entry so it loads.
Uses the local pnpm patch mechanism and rejects upstream edits.
The stub applies only to win32, the semaphore lock stays in use, and POSIX keeps native flock.
